en: Homage to the Lion of the Śākyas, the One Named in Eight Hundred Verses. O Perfectly Awakened One, lotus-eyed one, omniscient one, abode of compassion!

I bow to the Teacher Samantabhadra, the Lion of the Śākyas. I bow to the one who is a mass of glory, the glorious and most excellent one, the heap of virtue, the bringer of auspiciousness, the majestic one, the maker of glory, the peaceful one, and the one of peaceful appearance.
3. I bow to the proponent of selflessness, who is established, faultless, untainted, skilled in logic, pure in nature, and stainless. 4.
To the Tathāgata, who is beyond dispute, free from ego, and devoid of conceptual construction.
I bow to the one who has shaken off all afflictions, who is free from conceptual proliferation; I bow to the Lord of the Universe, the knower of liberation, the Leader of universal form.
I bow to the one who is fully endowed with the characteristics of the universe, who is free from passion.
6. I bow to the Lord of the Universe, perfected in knowledge and conduct, of stainless radiance, modest in appearance, vast, and free from all defects.
7. [I bow] to the Sage, the son of Śuddhodana, the subduer of the difficult-to-tame, the all-pervading, the pure.
O Sugata, O one of happy destiny, O gentle one of radiant fame, I bow to you! O Lord of Yogins, O One Possessed of the Ten Powers, O Knower of the World, O One Honored by the World,
O Teacher of the World, O One Without Teacher, O Protector of the World, I bow to you!

9. I bow to him who is free from blemish, the enemy of Kama, the stainless one who possesses all arts, whose form is beautiful, the object of compassion, and who has the luster of gold. 10. [I bow] to the supreme reality, the supreme light, the highest, the Supreme Lord.
I bow to the Blessed One, the capable one who brings about existence and non-existence.
I bow to the one of great intelligence, great heroism, great supernormal knowledge, and great strength; to the one of great exertion, great fortitude, and mighty arms.
12. I bow to Amitābha, the primordial purifier of all, the unconquered and the infallible, the Lord who is measured and devoted to the welfare of others.
13. [I bow to him] who has conquered the four Māra-enemies, the knower of reality, the benefactor, the auspicious one.
O essence of beings, O one of virtuous conduct, O caravan leader, I bow to you.
O God of gods, O Great God, O imperishable one worshipped by the gods, O Lord of gods who transcends all measures, O one of divine form, I bow to you.
15. I bow down to the Lord of Victors, the Supreme among Men, who has conquered his senses and conquered his afflictions—the most excellent, the best of beings, the Brahman, the field of merit.
16. Whatever person, having risen early in the morning, should recite this daily with devotion, [attains the highest goal].
This *Nāmāṣṭaśataka* is meritorious, purifying, and the destroyer of sins. (17) He shall obtain immeasurable enjoyments, both those of the earth and those arising in heaven;
diseases do not afflict him, and his bad dreams perish.
Endowed with long life and health, possessed of all sovereign powers,
intelligent, well-born, and eloquent, one shall become so in birth after birth by means of this *Nāmāṣṭaśataka*.
